est_basis: Team assumption, needs agronomist sign-off. PAU says the first nitrogen split goes with the first irrigation and gives the second split as 50-55 days after sowing, but no day count for the first irrigation. 21 to 28 days after sowing (3 to 4 weeks) is the usual timing.
Team assumption, needs agronomist sign-off. PAU names the knee-high stage without a day count. About 4 to 5 weeks after sowing; PAU's leaf colour chart for maize starts at 21 to 28 days after sowing.
Team assumption, needs agronomist sign-off. PAU names the pre-tasseling stage without a day count. About 7 to 8 weeks after sowing, before silking starts.
Team assumption, needs agronomist sign-off. PAU says half the nitrogen goes on at thinning without a day count. About 3 to 4 weeks after sowing.

Team assumption, needs agronomist sign-off. PAU says the other half goes on when flowers appear, without a day count. Squaring is 45 to 55 days after sowing (PAU), so flowers appear about 60 to 75 days.

Team assumption, needs agronomist sign-off. PAU says half the nitrogen goes on with the first irrigation after germination, without a day count; for autumn planting PAU gives the first irrigation one month after planting.
Team assumption, needs agronomist sign-off. PAU says the remaining half goes on in May or June. For a March planting that is about 60 to 120 days after planting.
